slot.brief: A particle moves with constant velocity along a straight line off-setting the origin; ask for the magnitude and direction of its angular momentum about a specified fixed point, and whether it changes along the path.

stem: A particle of mass $3\ \text{kg}$ has position vector $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j)\ \text{m}$ relative to a fixed point O at $t=0$, and moves with constant velocity $\vec v=(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Which option gives its angular momentum about O and its time dependence?
options: $\vec L=(12\hat i-6\hat j-15\hat k)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, with magnitude $9\sqrt5\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$; it remains constant.
$\vec L=(-12\hat i+6\hat j+15\hat k)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, with magnitude $9\sqrt5\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$; it remains constant.
$\vec L=(12\hat i-6\hat j+15\hat k)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, with magnitude $9\sqrt5\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$; it remains constant.
$\vec L=(12\hat i-6\hat j-15\hat k)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, with magnitude $9\sqrt5\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$; its magnitude changes along the path.

verdicts.working: \(\vec L=\vec r\times m\vec v=(1,2,0)\times(6,-3,6)=(12,-6,-15)\). Its magnitude is \(9\sqrt5\), and \(\vec r(t)\times m\vec v=\vec r_0\times m\vec v\), so it is constant.

working:
$\vec p=m\vec v=(6\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k)\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}$. $\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p=(12\hat i-6\hat j-15\hat k)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$; $|\vec L|=\sqrt{12^2+(-6)^2+(-15)^2}=9\sqrt5\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$. $\dfrac{d\vec L}{dt}=\vec v\times m\vec v=0$.

Independent check: \(\vec L=\vec r\times m\vec v=(1,2,0)\times(6,-3,6)=(12,-6,-15)\). Its magnitude is \(9\sqrt5\), and \(\vec r(t)\times m\vec v=\vec r_0\times m\vec v\), so it is constant.
